Paper pack · one-to-one check-in

Montree
Milestones

A developmental check-in for a Montessori classroom. Three times a year, about fifteen minutes, one adult and one child, in a quiet place. For the child it is simply Discovery Time: looking at pictures and talking with a grown-up they know.

4 years · A4 · 4;0 – 4;11

Form A — the paper pack for the Autumn and Spring windows. Three modules: Word & Sound Play, Number & Shape Play, English Time. 50 items in the sitting plus 6 practice items, 28 observation records rated across the whole window, and count-only summary tables.

Before you begin

How a check-in runs

Sit beside the child in a quiet space — never on the open work floor. Put the child pages where the child can see and reach them. You read; the child points, touches or talks; you mark the record sheet. Nothing is timed. Nothing here is a test of the child.

What is in this pack

  1. This guide — how to run the sitting.
  2. Teacher script, one block per item, for all three modules. Read the lines in quotation marks exactly as written — they are word-for-word the lines the tablet speaks, which is what keeps the two ways of running a check-in comparable.
  3. Child pages — the pictures the child looks at. No words and no instructions on them: everything the child hears comes from you.
  4. Record sheets, one per module, carrying the response key.
  5. Observation booklet — the records for this age, rated from what you have already seen in the work cycle, with the neighbouring ages printed for reference.
  6. Summary sheet — count-only lookup tables, then the numbers you type into Montree.

Printing and preparing

  • Print A4, single-sided, at 100% — no “fit to page”, because the pictures are sized for small hands.
  • Black-and-white printing is fine. Every picture stays readable in grey, apart from the 1 colour item listed a page or two on.
  • Separate the child pages from the teacher pages before you sit down — a folder or ring-binder, pictures facing the child, works well.
  • Keep the record sheet on your side of the table, angled away from the child.

The three modules

ModuleStrandsItems PracticeLength
Word & Sound Play
M-LIT		 Receptive language & listening · Expressive language & vocabulary · Phonological awareness · Print & alphabet knowledge 16 2 ≤5 min
Number & Shape Play
M-MATH		 Number sense & counting · Quantity, comparison & early operations · Shape, space & pattern · Measurement, sorting & classification 16 2 ≤5 min
English Time
M-EFL		 Receptive vocabulary (English) · Listening & instruction-following (English) · Phonological awareness (English) · Letter–sound knowledge (English) · Word reading / CVC (English) · Spoken production (English) 18 2 ≤5 min

The three modules together make one sitting of about fifteen minutes. You may run one module today and another tomorrow: a profile may be built across several days inside the same check-in window, and a part-finished sitting is still good information.

The rules of the sitting

Four things that matter more than the items

Practice first

Every module opens with two practice items. These are the only place you may tell the child how they are doing: a warm “yes, that’s the one”, or “let’s look at that one together” and show them. Practice is never recorded.

Then: warm, and even

Once the module proper begins, meet every answer the same way — “Thank you.” A nod, a smile, on to the next picture. The child must not be able to read from your face how it is going.

Repeating

If the child asks, say the line once more, exactly as written. Do not rephrase it, do not point, do not lean towards a picture. Then wait again.

Waiting

There is no time limit and no timer anywhere in this pack. Three- and four-year-olds often take several seconds before they commit to a choice. Let the silence sit.

When to stop

  • Within a strand — after 3 responses in a row that do not match the key, move on to the next strand. The remaining items in that strand are left blank and reported as not yet checked.
  • Across the module — after 5 in a row that do not match, close the module warmly and stop. “Thank you for playing with me today.”
  • Whenever the child has had enough — a child who wants to stop, stops. Note it on the record sheet and the profile stands as it is.

When a child sails through

If every item in a strand matches the key, you may carry on in that same strand with up to 4 items from the next age band’s pack, and note them on the record sheet under next-band items. This is how “already secure beyond this age” is evidenced — it is never assumed from a full sheet on its own.

Closing

Every child finishes the same way, whatever happened in between: “Thank you for playing with me today.” No stickers, no stars, no points to collect. A child should leave the table feeling exactly as good as the child who sat there before them.

About Form A and Form B

This is Form A, the form for the Autumn and Spring windows. Both forms exist on paper, one pack each: Form A for Autumn and Spring, Form B for Winter. They are matched strand by strand and carry the same number of items in the same order; only the pictures and the words change.

Use the pack that belongs to the window you are in, and record the form exactly as it is printed here — never relabel one form as the other. The whole point of two forms is that a child does not meet the same items twice in one year: repeating Form A in Winter would show practice, not growth, and the two windows could no longer honestly be read side by side.

What the words on the record sheet mean

EmergingThe beginnings are there, with an adult alongside.
DevelopingDoing it, most days, sometimes needing a hand.
SecureDoing it independently and consistently.
Not yet checkedToo little evidence this window. Reported openly, never hidden, and never counted as a difficulty.

Printing notice

These items need colour

Almost everything here prints perfectly well in black and white. The items below are the exception: colour is what is being asked about, so a grey print would change the question. Print those child pages on a colour printer, or leave the items blank and mark them not yet checked.

ItemStrandThe line you read
IT.E1.A4.A.05Receptive vocabulary (English)Red. Tap the red one.

Every other item is tagged as staying identifiable in greyscale, and no other item can be answered by colour alone.

Section 3

Child pages

The pages the child sees. There are no words on them on purpose: everything the child hears comes from you, so what is being looked at is listening and thinking, never reading.

Take these pages out and keep them in a folder facing the child. The small code at the foot of each page — module and item number — matches the number in the teacher script; it is there for you, not for the child. Some pages show one picture on its own at the top with choices underneath: the top picture is the one you draw the child’s attention to first, exactly as the script says.

Observation booklet — 4 years

Rate from what you have seen in the work cycle this term. Best fit, not a checklist. Leave a milestone unrated rather than guessing — unrated milestones are reported, never hidden.

These 28 records are not a sitting. They are the things you already know about a child from the work cycle — pouring, buttoning, joining a friend, staying with a hard job. Nothing here should be staged for the occasion. Tick the one description that fits best.

ATL-A.A4.1 Stays with a chosen work through a whole work cycle.

emerging Stays for part of the cycle before moving on.
developing Stays with one work for most of the cycle.
secure Works through the whole cycle and finishes what they began.

What you saw (optional)

developing Tries again once or twice, sometimes with encouragement.

What you saw (optional)

emerging Returns to the same easy work each day.

secure Chooses harder work themselves and enjoys the challenge.

3 years · A3 · reference only, not for ticking

Approaches to Learning & Self-Regulation

ATL-A.A3.1 Settles to a chosen activity for a short time.
emerging — Settles with an adult beside them for a moment or two. · developing — Settles to a chosen activity for a few minutes on most days. · secure — Settles quickly and stays until the activity feels finished.

ATL-A.A3.2 Comes back to an activity after a small interruption.
emerging — Needs an adult to lead them back. · developing — Comes back after a reminder. · secure — Comes back alone and picks up where they stopped.

ATL-B.A3.1 Chooses an activity with a little help.
emerging — Chooses when an adult offers two options. · developing — Chooses from the shelf with a gentle prompt. · secure — Chooses freely from the work they know.

ATL-B.A3.2 Shows what they want to do by pointing or asking.
emerging — Shows what they want by reaching or leading an adult. · developing — Points to or names the work they want. · secure — Asks clearly for the work or lesson they want.

ATL-C.A3.1 Tries a different way when something does not work.
emerging — Stops, or hands the work to an adult. · developing — Tries a second way after a suggestion. · secure — Tries several ways before asking for help.

ATL-C.A3.2 Uses a familiar material in a new way during play.
emerging — Uses the material only as it was shown. · developing — Adds a small change of their own. · secure — Invents new ways and explains them.

ATL-D.A3.1 Waits for a short turn with help from an adult.
emerging — Finds waiting hard even with support. · developing — Waits a short time with an adult nearby. · secure — Waits calmly for a short turn.

ATL-D.A3.2 Stops an action when reminded.
emerging — Needs to be gently moved away. · developing — Stops after one or two reminders. · secure — Stops at the first reminder.

Social & Emotional Development

SED-A.A3.1 Seeks out a familiar adult for comfort or help.
emerging — Accepts comfort when it is offered. · developing — Goes to a familiar adult when upset. · secure — Goes to a familiar adult and says what has upset them.

SED-A.A3.2 Responds warmly when an adult greets them.
emerging — Notices the greeting. · developing — Returns the greeting with a look or a word. · secure — Greets warmly, and often greets first.

SED-B.A3.1 Plays alongside other children happily.
emerging — Plays near others but mostly watches. · developing — Plays alongside others comfortably. · secure — Plays alongside and swaps a few words or materials.

SED-B.A3.2 Notices when another child is nearby and makes room.
emerging — Needs a reminder to make space. · developing — Makes room when asked. · secure — Notices and makes room without being asked.

SED-C.A3.1 Shows their feelings clearly and can be comforted.
emerging — Shows strong feelings and needs a lot of comfort. · developing — Shows feelings and settles with comfort. · secure — Shows feelings and settles quickly.

SED-C.A3.2 Recognises happy and sad in faces and stories.
emerging — Notices a strong feeling in a face. · developing — Points to happy or sad when asked. · secure — Names happy and sad and says why.

SED-D.A3.1 Copies a greeting with a familiar adult or child.
emerging — Watches the greeting. · developing — Copies the greeting when prompted. · secure — Greets by copying, without a prompt.

SED-D.A3.2 Begins to use please and thank you with reminders.
emerging — Uses them when they are said first. · developing — Uses them after a reminder. · secure — Uses them most of the time.

Language, Communication & Literacy

LCL-E.A3.1 Draws on purpose and says what it means.
emerging — Draws freely, without meaning attached. · developing — Says what a drawing means when asked. · secure — Draws something and tells you what it says.

LCL-E.A3.2 Draws lines, circles and shapes with growing control.
emerging — Scribbles with whole-arm movement. · developing — Draws lines and circles on purpose. · secure — Draws recognisable shapes on request.

Cognition: Mathematics & Exploration

COG-E.A3.1 Notices and points out changes around them.
emerging — Notices when it is pointed out. · developing — Points out changes they notice. · secure — Notices changes and talks about them.

COG-E.A3.2 Explores materials with all their senses.
emerging — Explores by looking and touching. · developing — Explores with several senses. · secure — Explores carefully and describes what they notice.

Physical Development & Practical Life

PPL-A.A3.1 Uses a whole-hand or three-finger grip to hold a tool.
emerging — Holds with a whole-hand grip. · developing — Uses a three-finger grip some of the time. · secure — Uses a three-finger grip comfortably.

PPL-A.A3.2 Threads large beads or uses tongs to move objects.
emerging — Manages with hand-over-hand help. · developing — Manages a few on their own. · secure — Threads or transfers a whole set smoothly.

PPL-B.A3.1 Walks, runs and climbs with growing steadiness.
emerging — Moves steadily on flat ground. · developing — Runs and climbs with growing confidence. · secure — Moves confidently over different surfaces.

PPL-B.A3.2 Carries a tray or a jug across the room without spilling.
emerging — Carries with an adult’s hand. · developing — Carries a light tray alone. · secure — Carries a full jug carefully across the room.

PPL-C.A3.1 Washes and dries hands with a reminder.
emerging — Washes with an adult guiding. · developing — Washes and dries after a reminder. · secure — Washes and dries thoroughly by themselves.

PPL-C.A3.2 Puts on shoes or a coat with some help.
emerging — Holds out arms and feet to be dressed. · developing — Manages part of it alone. · secure — Manages shoes or coat with only fastenings left.

PPL-D.A3.1 Helps put a material back on the shelf.
emerging — Puts it back when it is handed to them. · developing — Puts it back after a reminder. · secure — Puts it back in the right place by themselves.

PPL-D.A3.2 Wipes a spill when shown.
emerging — Watches an adult wipe. · developing — Wipes with help. · secure — Fetches the cloth and wipes alone.

5 years · A5 · reference only, not for ticking

Approaches to Learning & Self-Regulation

ATL-A.A5.1 Returns to the same work over several days to make it better.
emerging — Returns when reminded of the work. · developing — Returns over two or three days. · secure — Returns across the week, refining the work unprompted.

ATL-A.A5.2 Plans what they want to finish and sees it through.
emerging — Says what they want to do but changes often. · developing — Plans and finishes with an adult checking in. · secure — Plans, gathers what is needed, and finishes independently.

ATL-B.A5.1 Plans their morning and chooses a balance of work.
emerging — Plans one work at a time. · developing — Plans two or three works with support. · secure — Plans a balanced morning across areas independently.

ATL-B.A5.2 Asks for a new lesson when they are ready for one.
emerging — Watches other children’s lessons with interest. · developing — Asks for a lesson when reminded it is available. · secure — Asks for the next lesson at the right moment for themselves.

ATL-C.A5.1 Thinks a problem through before acting.
emerging — Acts first, then notices the problem. · developing — Pauses and thinks when reminded. · secure — Pauses, plans, then acts.

ATL-C.A5.2 Explains how they solved something to another child.
emerging — Shows another child what to do. · developing — Explains with a few words and gestures. · secure — Explains the steps clearly so the other child can follow.

ATL-D.A5.1 Waits, takes turns and follows the ground rules without reminders.
emerging — Follows the rules with reminders. · developing — Follows the rules for most of the day. · secure — Follows the rules all day and helps others to.

ATL-D.A5.2 Calms themselves when upset, using a strategy they know.
emerging — Needs an adult to help them settle. · developing — Uses a known strategy when reminded. · secure — Notices the feeling and settles themselves.

Social & Emotional Development

SED-A.A5.1 Talks with adults about ideas and plans, not only needs.
emerging — Talks mostly about what they need. · developing — Talks about what they are making or doing. · secure — Talks about ideas and plans and asks the adult’s view.

SED-A.A5.2 Accepts guidance from an adult and acts on it.
emerging — Accepts guidance reluctantly. · developing — Accepts and follows guidance most times. · secure — Accepts guidance readily and puts it to use.

SED-B.A5.1 Works with others on a shared plan.
emerging — Works beside others on the same thing. · developing — Agrees a simple plan with one child. · secure — Plans with a group and shares out the roles.

SED-B.A5.2 Sorts out a small disagreement with words.
emerging — Comes to an adult to settle it. · developing — Uses words with an adult nearby. · secure — Settles small disagreements independently.

SED-C.A5.1 Talks about why they feel a certain way.
emerging — Names the feeling only. · developing — Gives a simple reason. · secure — Explains the reason and what would help.

SED-C.A5.2 Offers comfort or help to a child who is upset.
emerging — Watches with concern. · developing — Offers help when it is suggested. · secure — Offers comfort in their own way, unprompted.

SED-D.A5.1 Uses the classroom courtesies naturally through the day.
emerging — Uses courtesies at set moments. · developing — Uses courtesies through much of the day. · secure — Courtesy is part of how they move through the day.

SED-D.A5.2 Helps a younger child learn a routine.
emerging — Notices a younger child needing help. · developing — Helps when asked. · secure — Helps a younger child patiently and unprompted.

Language, Communication & Literacy

LCL-E.A5.1 Writes their own name clearly.
emerging — Writes their name with a model to copy. · developing — Writes their name from memory, letters uneven. · secure — Writes their name clearly and consistently.

LCL-E.A5.2 Writes short taught words using the sounds they know.
emerging — Writes the first sound of a word only. · developing — Writes the first and last sounds. · secure — Writes short taught words readably.

Cognition: Mathematics & Exploration

COG-E.A5.1 Makes a guess about what will happen and checks it.
emerging — Says what they think will happen. · developing — Guesses and watches what happens. · secure — Guesses, checks, and says whether they were right.

COG-E.A5.2 Talks about living things, the weather or the seasons with some detail.
emerging — Names a plant, animal or weather word. · developing — Describes one of them in a sentence. · secure — Explains a change and gives a reason.

Physical Development & Practical Life

PPL-A.A5.1 Draws and writes with steady control.
emerging — Lines are large and uneven. · developing — Control is steady for short pieces. · secure — Control is steady and sized to the paper.

PPL-A.A5.2 Fastens buttons, zips and small catches.
emerging — Manages large fastenings with help. · developing — Manages most fastenings alone. · secure — Manages all the classroom fastenings independently.

PPL-B.A5.1 Hops, skips and changes direction with control.
emerging — Hops on the spot. · developing — Hops and skips a short distance. · secure — Hops, skips and turns with control.

PPL-B.A5.2 Carries and places heavy or awkward material safely.
emerging — Carries light material alone. · developing — Carries heavier material with care. · secure — Judges what they can carry and asks for help when needed.

PPL-C.A5.1 Looks after their own belongings all day.
emerging — Needs reminders about belongings. · developing — Keeps track of belongings on most days. · secure — Keeps belongings in order without reminders.

PPL-C.A5.2 Notices what they need and gets it themselves.
emerging — Tells an adult what they need. · developing — Gets what they need when reminded where it is. · secure — Notices and gets what they need independently.

PPL-D.A5.1 Takes care of the room without being asked.
emerging — Tidies when asked. · developing — Notices and tidies their own area. · secure — Notices what the room needs and does it.

PPL-D.A5.2 Shows another child how to care for a material.
emerging — Tells a child not to spoil a material. · developing — Shows a child what to do when asked. · secure — Shows a child carefully and patiently, unprompted.

Canopy · G1 · reference only, not for ticking

Approaches to Learning & Self-Regulation

ATL-A.G1.1 Works with deep focus on one activity for a long stretch.
emerging — Stays with an activity for a few minutes before moving on. · developing — Works for a good stretch and comes back after a short break. · secure — Works right through a long stretch and would rather not be interrupted.

ATL-A.G1.2 Picks up work begun on another day and carries it through to the end.
emerging — Starts again from the beginning, or leaves it. · developing — Picks it up again once someone reminds them where they stopped. · secure — Finds their own work, sees where they stopped, and finishes it.

ATL-B.G1.1 Chooses their own work and begins it without being told.
emerging — Waits to be pointed towards something. · developing — Chooses on most days, with a word from an adult now and then. · secure — Comes in, decides, and begins on their own.

ATL-B.G1.2 Asks a question when they are unsure what to do, instead of stopping.
emerging — Goes quiet or waits when stuck. · developing — Asks once an adult comes near. · secure — Seeks someone out and asks a clear question.

ATL-C.G1.1 Tries a way of their own before asking an adult for help.
emerging — Asks for help as soon as something is hard. · developing — Tries once, then asks. · secure — Tries more than one way, and can say what they tried.

ATL-C.G1.2 Looks back over their own work and puts right whatever does not look right.
emerging — Says it is finished without looking back over it. · developing — Looks back when asked, and changes what an adult points out. · secure — Looks back without being asked and puts things right on their own.

ATL-D.G1.1 Moves calmly from one activity to the next with little help.
emerging — Needs an adult alongside them at each change. · developing — Moves on with a reminder, and settles again quickly. · secure — Finishes, tidies and moves on without being prompted.

ATL-D.G1.2 Waits their turn and holds back a first impulse when the moment calls for it.
emerging — Acts straight away and finds waiting hard. · developing — Waits with a reminder, for a short time. · secure — Waits, and stops themselves without anyone saying anything.

Social & Emotional Development

SED-A.G1.1 Talks with a familiar adult about their own work and what they are trying to do.
emerging — Answers a direct question about the work. · developing — Shows the work and says a little about it. · secure — Starts the conversation and explains what they are aiming for.

SED-A.G1.2 Asks an adult for what they need, in words, at a good moment.
emerging — Shows what they need without words, or waits. · developing — Asks, but often breaks in on something else. · secure — Waits for a good moment and asks clearly.

SED-B.G1.1 Takes turns in a group activity without an adult reminding them.
emerging — Takes turns when an adult manages it. · developing — Takes turns with an occasional reminder. · secure — Keeps the turns going, and helps others keep them too.

SED-B.G1.2 Builds on what another child has just said in a conversation.
emerging — Talks alongside others rather than to them. · developing — Answers a peer, then moves to their own subject. · secure — Picks up a peer’s idea and adds to it across several exchanges.

SED-C.G1.1 Names how they feel with a word that fits, not only happy or sad.
emerging — Uses happy or sad for most feelings. · developing — Finds a more exact word with a little help. · secure — Chooses a word that fits, and says what brought the feeling on.

SED-C.G1.2 Uses a way of their own to settle when they are upset.
emerging — Needs an adult to settle them. · developing — Uses a familiar way when reminded of it. · secure — Chooses a way and uses it without being asked.

SED-D.G1.1 Greets, thanks and asks politely without being prompted.
emerging — Uses courteous words when reminded. · developing — Uses them with familiar people most of the time. · secure — Uses them with everyone, including visitors, unprompted.

SED-D.G1.2 Settles a small disagreement with a friend using words.
emerging — Comes to an adult with the disagreement. · developing — Talks it through with an adult nearby. · secure — Talks it through with the other child on their own.

Language, Communication & Literacy

LCL-E.G1.1 Writes a sentence of their own with a capital letter, spaces between the words and a full stop.
emerging — Writes words, with the spaces or the capital letter still coming. · developing — Writes a sentence with most of the punctuation in place. · secure — Writes a sentence with the capital, the spaces and the full stop all in place.

LCL-E.G1.2 Writes a short piece of two or more sentences that holds together from beginning to end.
emerging — Writes one sentence at a time, each on its own. · developing — Writes two or three sentences on one subject. · secure — Writes a short piece with a clear beginning and a closing idea.

Cognition: Mathematics & Exploration

COG-E.G1.1 Asks a question about the world and suggests a way to find out.
emerging — Notices something and says what they see. · developing — Asks a question about it. · secure — Asks a question and suggests how they could find out.

COG-E.G1.2 Keeps a simple record of what they notice and says what it shows.
emerging — Talks about what they noticed without recording it. · developing — Draws or tallies what they noticed. · secure — Records it in a chart or tally and says what it shows.

Physical Development & Practical Life

PPL-A.G1.1 Forms letters and numerals starting in the right place and moving in the right direction.
emerging — Forms them recognisably, starting in various places. · developing — Forms most of them the right way round. · secure — Forms letters and numerals correctly and comfortably, at speed.

PPL-A.G1.2 Uses scissors and other classroom tools accurately and safely.
emerging — Uses a tool with an adult alongside. · developing — Uses familiar tools on their own, roughly accurately. · secure — Uses tools accurately, and puts them away safely.

PPL-B.G1.1 Throws, catches or kicks with control in a game.
emerging — Sends and stops a ball at close range. · developing — Catches or kicks accurately most of the time. · secure — Keeps control of the ball inside a game with others.

PPL-B.G1.2 Puts movements together — hopping, skipping, jumping — and keeps their balance.
emerging — Performs one movement at a time. · developing — Links two movements with a pause between. · secure — Links several movements smoothly, staying balanced.

PPL-C.G1.1 Looks after their own belongings and personal care without an adult.
emerging — Manages with a step-by-step reminder. · developing — Manages most of it independently. · secure — Manages it all, and notices when something is missing.

PPL-C.G1.2 Gets themselves ready for what comes next without being told.
emerging — Follows the group once it has started moving. · developing — Gets ready with a reminder. · secure — Sees what is coming and gets ready on their own.

PPL-D.G1.1 Sets up what they need and clears it all away afterwards.
emerging — Clears away when asked. · developing — Sets up and clears away with a reminder. · secure — Sets up, clears away and leaves the space ready for the next child.

PPL-D.G1.2 Keeps up a job for the classroom right across the week.
emerging — Does the job on the day they are reminded. · developing — Does it most days of the week. · secure — Does it every day without being reminded.

Section 6

Lookup & summary

Point counts become bands by reading a row. Then the counts go into Montree, which writes the family’s Growth Story.

Section 6 · counting only

From the sheets to the bands

Add up the points you marked for each milestone’s items, then read the band straight off the row. The cut-offs are already worked out — there is nothing to divide and no percentage to work out. If fewer items were given than the last column asks for, the milestone is not yet checked: leave it, and it is reported as it stands. A dash means that band cannot arise for a milestone carrying that few points.

Your judgement comes last, and it wins. If the band the table gives you does not match the child you know, set the band you believe is right and write one line saying why. Montree keeps both and reports how often it happened, openly, as a count. This pack supports teacher observation; it does not overrule it.

What this age is expected to reach

At 4 years this pack carries 44 core milestones marked expected and 8 in English. A further 1 belongs to the band above — securing it is recorded as exceeded. 3 are informative rather than expected: they appear in some children at this age and are never counted against a child. Only expected milestones that were actually checked go into the attainment figure; everything left blank is printed as not yet checked, never quietly dropped.

Type these into Montree

Core: secure · developing · emerging · not yet checked
English: secure · developing · emerging · not yet checked
Milestones secured from the band above (exceeded)
Bands you set yourself, against the table

Montree turns these counts into the family’s Growth Story and into the attainment figure — the share of the milestones typically expected at this age in mainstream early-years settings that this child has securely met, always printed with the number it was counted out of. Where fewer than 12 expected milestones were checked, no percentage is shown at all and the milestone list stands on its own. There are no percentiles, no ranking of one child against another, and no comparison of one class with another.

A note for whoever reads this next

These are criterion-referenced classroom check-ins carried out by the child’s own teacher. They are not psychometrically normed instruments; the two forms are matched by design rather than by calibration; and one classroom is far too small a group to draw norms from. What they carry honestly is this child’s own movement, window to window — which is the evidence worth having.
